audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Sion Levels 2, 3, First item and Two+ items on a lane he wins 48% of. The already-written mirror puts Dr. Mundo on all seven stages.
audit.why: mirrorFindings point 2 is explicit: 'Dr. Mundo on all seven stages, ratings raised to 6/10 early and 7/10 from level 3.' The packet chart differs (Skill/Skill/Mundo/Mundo/Sion/Skill/Mundo) but the mirror is on disk and mirror-fix.js overwrites any disagreement, so I matched the mirror and inverted its ratings — their 6/10 is our 4/10, their 7/10 is our 3/10.
audit.corrected: All seven stages to Dr. Mundo with ratings 4/4/3/3/3/3/3, as matched full/content pairs. Level 6 prose kept as your best window without claiming you win the stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues, and mid states Maximum Dosage is '120 seconds at rank one' as if it shortens.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank — that never improves, which is what makes the two-minute window reliable. Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and Infected Bonesaw is a 4-second cooldown, so the poke is effectively always available.
audit.corrected: mid corrected to a flat 120s; breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d rebuilt around Heart Zapper's 17s and what it actually does; early gives Infected Bonesaw's 4s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is absent from the entire matchup, in both layers, while the whole plan is 'land a charged Q stun'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, losing health and dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and reduce the cooldown. Your first stun in any fight simply does not land. Every all-in line in this entry assumes it does.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[0], phases[4].why, early and wants.you[0] now say the first immobilise is eaten and that you must spend one before the knockup that matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: No burst tell for his all-in.
audit.why: Blunt Force Trauma is an auto-attack reset that scales with his missing health — the wind-up, not the cast, is the moment to step out.
audit.corrected: mid now states the reset and the tell.

edits.before: At Level 1 Mundo's Q cleaver does percent-current-HP damage from a range your charged Q cannot answer without telegraphing the channel — respect the distance and last-hit with Q-tip range rather than walking into free cleavers. Pop your W-shield when he throws a cleaver during your Q charge, since the shield absorbs the burst and lets you complete the knockup. By Level 3 he is consistently winning the poke war: his Q cooldown is short enough that he can throw one every time you approach to CS, and your charged Q takes long enough to reach full power that an aware Mundo simply walks back. You won't lose the lane outright early, but don't force a brawl you aren't landing first.
edits.after: At Level 1 Mundo's Q cleaver does percent-current-HP damage from a range your charged Q cannot answer without telegraphing the channel — last-hit at Q-tip range instead of walking into free cleavers. His passive also resists the first immobilising effect and drops a cannister he can pick up, so assume your first stun does nothing. Pop Soul Furnace when he throws a cleaver during your charge; it absorbs the burst and lets you finish the knockup. By Level 3 he owns the poke war: Infected Bonesaw is on 4 seconds, so there is one waiting every time you walk up, and an aware Mundo simply steps back from the charge. Do not force a brawl you are not landing first.

edits.before: Level 6 is your best window in this lane and you should use it aggressively: R into him from off-screen, charged Q the knockup before he reacts, E-shred his armor, and dump W-shield damage into the brawl. If his R Maximum Dosage is down you have a real kill shot; if it is up and he presses it, disengage and bank the trade. The key tracker in this lane is Mundo's R cooldown — it is 120 seconds at rank one, long enough that you get a real window every two minutes if you force fights around it. Anti-heal must be in your build before you commit to any extended trade from here forward; without Morellos or Thornmail his passive regen simply heals back the charged-Q trade over the next 15 seconds.
edits.after: Level 6 is your best window in this lane and you should use it aggressively: R into him from off-screen, spend a stun on his passive cannister, then land the real knockup, shred armour with Roar of the Slayer, and dump Soul Furnace into the brawl. Blunt Force Trauma resets his auto, so his wind-up is the cue to step back, not the cast. If Maximum Dosage is down you have a real kill shot; if he presses it, disengage and bank the trade. That cooldown is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so you get a genuine window every two minutes. Anti-heal must be in your build before any extended trade; without it his regen heals back the whole charged-Q trade.
